facts.statement: The fossils come from the Eifelian stage of the Devonian period.
The type locality of Yipetalichthys is the Shangshuanghe Formation in China.
facts.quote:
Type locality: Shangshuanghe Formation
Country: China

facts.statement: Yipetalichthys was described in a 2026 paper in the journal Papers in Palaeontology by Zhaohui Pan and colleagues.
facts.quote:
Study title: A new quasipetalichthyid placoderm from the Middle Devonian of China
Journal: Papers in Palaeontology
Year: 2026
Authors: Zhaohui Pan, Vincent Dupret, Per E. Ahlberg, Wenjin Zhao, Jianhua Wang, Mengjun Wang, Min Zhu

facts.statement: High‑resolution micro‑CT scans show that Yipetalichthys possessed an endocranium with cranial nerve grooves and inner‑ear structures.

The dermal neck joint of Yipetalichthys allows measurement of the angle between the ventral laminar ridge and the skull‑roof midline, which in known specimens falls into two non‑overlapping ranges: ≤15° or ≥28°.
Yipetalichthys exhibits a high ventral laminar ridge angle, supporting its placement in Quasipetalichthyidae.
Phylogenetic analysis places the order Petalichthyida as sister to Ptyctodontida and assigns Yipetalichthys to the family Quasipetalichthyidae.
Yipetalichthys possesses an elaborate sliding neck joint guided by a ventral laminar ridge that forms a longitudinal sliding track against the anterior dorsolateral plate.
Researchers note that the 15–28° angle interval is currently unsampled, leaving the threshold for distinguishing neck‑joint states open to future testing.
